items.title: Quantitative Global Macro Strategy: The Quality Factor
items.summary: We recap our case that the classic growth/inflation quadrant framework is incomplete, as levels alone fail to separate regimes cleanly in recessions and also in late-cycle periods, which we may be seeing now. We look at the closest historical analogues to today and offer further analysis.

items.title: NVIDIA Reinstates Jensen Huang
items.summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a move we see as removing a key overhang, though uncertainty remains about the investigation into Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence contact and Megaspeed-related export probes. We raise our target price to $240.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: Flows Driving EURUSD Over Fundamentals
items.summary: On Oct. 1 we flagged that EURUSD could reach 1.0850 on misvaluation alone, assuming unchanged relative real yields. Since then, relative real yields are at similar levels and EURUSD is actually now much closer to the 1.0850 area. Historically, such misvaluations tend to be short-lived.

items.title: Global Commodities: Broad-Based Selloff Is a Buying Opportunity
items.summary: Commodity markets' major and broad-based selloff has accelerated, reflecting a broader weakening in risk assets with cyclical equities dropping sharply, alongside a sharp tech equity pullback and a hawkish Fed. That presents a buying opportunity in agricultural commodities, as we discuss.

items.title: What Lies Ahead for Spain?
items.summary: We look at the economic outlook for Spain should elections bring a conservative PP-Vox alliance government to power, as expected. We see GDP overperformance continuing given a housing upswing and a supply-friendly policy mix. We offer further analysis of potential impacts in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Vodafone to Sell
items.summary: We're downgrading Vodafone to sell. German operations remain under pressure and significant debt consolidation related to the terms of Vodafone's new OXG partnership looms in the medium term. Moreover, despite recent share-price underperformance, we see yet more downside risk.

items.title: Five Big Debates About BT
items.summary: BT remains a divisive stock. Fiber investment is maturing, while the TalkTalk acquisition is modestly accretive. But competition remains tough in UK fixed line, and free-cash-flow consensus forecasts continue to fall. In this note we address five main discussion topics about Sell-rated BT.

items.title: Electrical Equipment Is Now Pricing In a Data-Center Plateau
items.summary: The sell-off in electrical-equipment stocks reflects a confluence of concerns ranging from data-center permitting and financing to export curbs on GPUs. We think data centers plateauing from 2027 is now priced in. We see the sub-sector as oversold, but with few catalysts into year's end.

items.title: U.S. Application Software: Previewing Our 10th Annual Cloud Forum
items.summary: Our 10th annual Cloud Forum will be held at AWS re:Invent on Nov. 30 in Las Vegas. We preview key themes in this note, including shifts in AI diffusion throughout software, harness and multi-model usage, cybersecurity, trends in enterprise tech spending, and more.

items.title: U.S. Economics: Rate Hikes in 2026 Set Up Rate Cuts in 2027
items.summary: Two-year Treasury yields fell along with equity prices as investors price in a higher likelihood of an AI-related investment slowdown, significantly cooling U.S. economic growth. Fed officials seem determined to raise rates 25 basis points in December, but we continue to expect 2027 cuts.

items.title: European Equity Strategy: From Defensives to Quality
items.summary: Equities have sold off with European Defensives sharply outperforming Cyclicals, raising questions about the sustainability of the current rotation and recent moves' macro significance. As we explore herein, our work suggests Quality may be a more interesting place to position from here.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: What to Call This?
items.summary: How to describe recent equity price action? We explore several likely explanations herein, but also note earnings expectations remain unchanged while our Levkovich Index has come off but remains in euphoria. This means valuations look increasingly compelling but may also be misleading.

items.title: U.S. Auto Manufacturers: BEV Update
items.summary: BEV share of the U.S. market seems to have stabilized at 6% of total U.S. light vehicle sales since March, but we think that share will move toward 10% over the next few years. In this note we dig more deeply into the numbers and explore California market's share as a useful indicator.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Hawks With Chips on Their Shoulders
items.summary: We expect the concerns around the AI selloff to at least restrain the Fed from hiking too quickly. With the hawkish Fed still driving the very front end of the curve, the belly of the curve should be more reactive to the risk-off sentiment. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Stay Cautious As Alarm Bells Get Louder
items.summary: AI risks have been rising, and NVDA's results didn't reassure the market. Under the hood, the factor and sector rotation has been extreme and reminiscent of 2000 and 2021, with our generals framework likely about to trigger. We offer suggested tactics in response to louder alarm bells.

items.title: North America Trucking: Key Takeaways From LTL Survey
items.summary: We hosted Mastio & Co. President Kevin Huntsman to discuss Mastio's widely followed survey on shipper perceptions of less-than-truckload carriers’ service and pricing/value. We note seven key takeaways from the survey and our discussion in this note.

items.title: U.S. REITs and Lodging: Takeaways From Nareit
items.summary: The mood at the Nareit conference was generally optimistic. Interest rates and the broad AI trade will continue to impact absolute performance, but REIT tailwinds are driven by a multi-year lower supply environment, solid KPIs and well-positioned balance sheets. We offer our takeaways.

items.title: Germany Can't "Outgrow" the Need for Consolidation
items.summary: In this month’s Germany Fiscal Monitor, we discuss why improved economic prospects go alongside wider rather than narrower deficits for now, and why higher growth will unlikely be sufficient to stabilize Germany's debt/GDP ratio.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Post-Midterms Shake-Out
items.summary: Since the U.S. midterms, risk sentiment has weakened sharply due to a host of stressors, explored in this note. We look at the potential impacts of factors — including sustained AI headwinds, lower energy prices and depressed commodity prices — on various emerging markets.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: Sizing Up Supply for 2027
items.summary: We analyze the 2027 gross and net supply in EGBs, SSAs, covered bonds and Gilts. In EGBs, € SSAs and covered bonds, we expect a marginal increase in gross supply to €2.2 trillion. However, we believe NCR for these assets is set to decrease by 13%. We offer further takeaways herein.

items.title: Oil Monitor: Geopolitical Tensions Remain Despite Oil Selloff
items.summary: Oil and diesel prices have both eased, due to factors explored herein. But renewed tensions point to another potential round of escalation, and Middle East exports' sustainability is uncertain. In this note we offer detailed tracking of oil flows around the Middle East, Russia and China.

items.title: Uranium Outlook: Can Producers Fill the Supply Gap?
items.summary: We continue to expect uranium to trade above $100 a pound over the next three months, as nuclear energy demand is set to continue growing. Producer costs have kept rising, and we see limited appetite among them to meaningfully scale production. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Walmart Reports Solid Third-Quarter Numbers
items.summary: Walmart reported solid third-quarter results and raised FY26 guidance modestly; we note four key positives from Buy-rated WMT's quarter. Looking to 2027, management remains confident despite transitory headwinds as new aspects of the business have higher profit margins.

items.title: EM Credit Weekly: The Macro Backdrop Still Warrants Caution
items.summary: We stay bearish on emerging-markets credit into year's end. Reaccelerating U.S. inflation and Fed tightening are keeping Treasury yields elevated, while a strong dollar adds to funding pressure and flows into the asset class. Favorable November-to-January seasonality is a risk to our call.

items.title: Australia's Labor Market Finally Starts to Loosen
items.summary: Australia's labor market loosened in October, with a clear underlying trend: There are ~80,000 fewer people employed since August, and the employment-to-population ratio is now below its early 2025 peak. We expect policymakers to hold rates steady until next year's third quarter.

items.title: We're Downgrading Transurban to Sell
items.summary: We're downgrading Transurban to Sell, with an A$13.90 target price. Soft October traffic growth indicates elevated fuel prices and cost-of-living pressures are hampering Australian road usage. TCL is trading in line with its historical ~4.5% dividend yield, likely leaving upside limited.

items.title: Correlation Corner: Between an Oil Shock and a Burst AI Bubble
items.summary: Cross-asset implied correlations are caught between pricing an oil supply shock and a burst AI bubble. For those looking to hedge equity downside, some of these dislocations from higher oil can provide good correlation entry levels for risk-off hedges. We highlight three opportunities.

items.title: Emerging Markets Credit Focus: 2027 Supply Outlook
items.summary: We forecast emerging-markets sovereign hard-currency gross issuance of $237 billion in 2027, down ~11% from 2026, with net supply remaining manageable. Sovereign technicals remain the more supportive of the two, while investment grade should continue to dominate corporate issuance.

items.title: U.S. Oil & Gas Exploration and Production: A Resilient Quarter
items.summary: Thie third-quarter E&P earnings season was characterized by strong operational execution and continued capital discipline, with companies largely topping production and cash-flow expectations, demonstrating resilience. In this note, we detail the key themes to emerge from the quarter.

items.title: We're Raising Our Forecasts for South Korea's Growth
items.summary: We raise our South Korea real GDP growth forecasts for 2026 through 2028,  underpinned by a larger contribution from the IT manufacturing sector amid a prolonged memory upcycle. We keep our terminal rate assumption at 3.5%, expecting moderating core inflation and still-weak consumption.

items.title: Ignite Shows Further Confidence in Microsoft's Growth Drivers
items.summary: Microsoft's Ignite conference reinforced its efforts to broaden AI monetization beyond Copilot, with announcements and management commentary increasingly focused on enterprise knowledge, autonomous agents, security, and AI infrastructure. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Siemens Remains a Physical AI Winner
items.summary: Siemens' valuation gap to peers has substantially closed, due to its own outperformance as well as the de-rating of electrical/data-center and software peers. As Siemens remains a major potential beneficiary of the physical AI theme, we stay Buy-rated and increase our target price to €340.

items.title: We're Downgrading New York Times to Neutral
items.summary: While we remain confident in New York Times’s long-term outlook, we explore six near-term trends we see as eroding, ranging from falling app downloads to decelerating monetization. As such, we are lowering our target price to $76 and downgrading New York Times to Neutral.

items.title: Latin America Local Markets Scanner: November
items.summary: Despite sustained market volatility, a common theme across Latin America remains local rates' inability to keep pace with Fed-led tightening in financial conditions, as currencies broadly weaken amid eroding rate differentials.  We offer country-by-country analysis and thoughts on tactics.

items.title: Singapore Equity Strategy: Position for Defensives vs. Cyclicals
items.summary: We rate Singapore Underweight relative to ASEAN into next year's first half, setting an STI target of 5,325. Positive catalysts seem largely priced in; we recommend rotating away from crowded cyclicals toward value and defensives, and our preference is for large caps over small caps.

items.title: Previewing Key Themes for Our Basic Materials Conference
items.summary: Our 18th annual Basic Materials Conference will be held Dec. 1-2 in New York City. We will host fireside chats with EMN, AXTA, Air Liquide, WLK, FUL, DOW and PPG. In this conference preview, we highlight key themes, explore our latest market views, and update our rank order.

items.title: Citi China Conference 2026: The Paradoxes of Chinese Consumption
items.summary: We hosted Steven Barnett, former IMF Senior Resident Representative, at our 2026 China Conference. He sees China's low consumption share as reflecting an exceptionally high savings rate, not a low household income share, and identifies consumption as a rising policy priority.

items.title: Brazil Equity Strategy: Earnings Wrap-Up
items.summary: Brazil's earnings season proved constructive overall, with 40 of 72 Ibovespa names posting positive earnings surprises and 32 beating on revenue. Importantly, analyst sentiment deteriorated only marginally after the country's elections and sits near the top of its historical range.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Conviction Remains Uneven
items.summary: Global positioning improved during the week, but the quality of flows differed materially across regions. In the U.S., much of the recovery was driven by short covering rather than new long flows, suggesting investor conviction remains limited. We offer further analysis in this note.
